chapter_note: This chapter has no cosmological substrate. The five-fold structure (Wisdom, Faith, [Perfection], Love, Patience) is a Manichaean ecclesial virtue-teaching about what the Light Mind produces in the Elect. Both sides of every mapping reach into the editor's contemporary church world — the Elect, the brothers and sisters seated together, the church (ⲧⲉⲕⲕⲗⲏⲥⲓⲁ), the New Man. Teaching purity score is 0.000, confirming this. The chapter is uniformly ecclesial-hortatory application material wrapped in the apostolic dialogue frame. The five-fold enumeration MIMICS the substrate's numbered correspondences but lists ethical virtues mapped onto institutional life rather than cosmos→cosmos correspondences. The "patience of the privation in secret which he bears in the church" (i=18) is explicitly ecclesial. Heavy damage (69%) but enough survives to identify the layer clearly.

segments.temporal_note: Chapter number marker — part of editorial apparatus.
Chapter title 'Concerning the five marvelous works' — editorial heading.
Title continuation — about what the Mind of Light habitually does.
'manifests forth in the elect' — ⲛⲉⲕⲗⲉⲕⲧⲟⲥ marks ecclesial frame. Mapping reaches into the contemporary Manichaean institution.
ⲧⲧⲁⲗⲓⲛ ⲁⲛ ⲡⲁϫⲉ ⲡⲁⲡⲟⲥⲧⲟⲗⲟⲥ — pure Manichaean dialogue attribution formula.
'produces five kinds of light in the elect' — five-fold structure tied directly to the Elect institution. The first is Wisdom — but Wisdom here is what the Elect proclaims, not a cosmic register.
Wisdom that 'the elect habitually proclaims' — proclamation is the Elect's institutional function (preaching to catechumens).
Continuation: 'in all her aspects, types, tropes' — describes the Elect's preaching, not cosmic structure.
'The second is faith' — virtue enumeration, not cosmic enumeration. Maps onto the proclamation context.
'after his proclamation of Wisdom which is being proclaimed' — proclamation context, ecclesial mission.
'that the others who hear her may have [faith] in her' — describes catechumen reception, ecclesial mission outcome.
'The third is...' — third virtue (lacuna), continues virtue enumeration in the ecclesial frame.
'in his proclamation... rest' — proclamation context continues.
'rest of heart for the gathering of his brothers' — explicit community/assembly reference. Ecclesial mapping.
'is love, that he habitually loves Wisdom' — love as institutional virtue toward fellow Elect.
'the brothers and the sisters who are seated in his midst' — explicit community gathering, brothers and sisters.
Fifth virtue: 'patience of the privation in secret' — ascetic-institutional virtue.
'those who have not received the hope of God' — describes outsiders relative to the church.
Explicit ⲧⲉⲕⲕⲗⲏⲥⲓⲁ — 'which he bears in the church as a privation'. Strongest ecclesial marker in the chapter.
'a privation in secret, on account of their foolishness' — continues ecclesial-ascetic frame.
'places these five kinds in the New Man' — ⲣⲙⲛⲃⲣⲣⲉ; the New Man is institutionalized soteriology, not cosmic substrate.
'purified, has chosen him, has set him on his feet' — initiation/election language.
Fragment with 'every man' — appears to begin generalizing application.
'These belong to every man' — universalizing pastoral/hortatory voice.
'the Mind meditates in his Wisdom' — continues ecclesial-spiritual reflection.
'these five kinds...' — final summary of the ecclesial virtue-list.
'shall be established within him and perfected within him' — perfection language tied to the Elect's spiritual progress.
'shall become an unfailing vessel and a pearl' — pastoral/exhortative metaphor (compare 'become good pearls' in framework examples).
'forever, that cannot be matched' — closing hortatory benediction.
